headline: Middle East petfood makers eye European markets at Pet World Arabia
deck: 208 exhibitors and 13,000 regional visitors at Dubai World Trade Centre put the focus on supply chains for petfood distribution across MENA.
excerpt: Pet World Arabia opens in Dubai on 13 September as the region's largest B2B pet industry exhibition. For MENA petfood manufacturers, the trade floor is the place to negotiate distribution with retailers, clinic chains and wholesalers across the Arab world and into Europe.
content:
Pet World Arabia opens at Dubai World Trade Centre on 13 September for two days, drawing 208 exhibitors and over 13,000 expected visitors across retail chains, wholesalers, veterinary clinics and distributors from the Middle East and Africa. The exhibition is run by Al Fajer Information & Services, which has organised regional trade shows since 1975.

The regional petfood market is projected to reach $6.13bn by end-2026, with compound annual growth rates of 4.2 percent through 2030. The manufacturers on the floor are positioned to capture export orders from established distribution networks. A significant share of the show's appeal to international participants stems from the opportunity to negotiate supply arrangements with established regional distribution networks spanning 30+ countries. Unlike European and North American petfood conferences, which focus on innovation and consumer trends, Pet World Arabia is a procurement event: manufacturers meet the buyers who stock their shelves across the MENA region and gateway markets into Africa and Asia.

Turkish exhibitors have been prominent in previous years, with strong participation from manufacturers diversifying supply chains away from single-source European suppliers. For Gulf-based producers in Saudi Arabia and the UAE, the show is a platform to test market acceptance of new premium formulations and to lock in supply commitments with regional retail chains ahead of the post-summer retail season. New entrants from Pakistan and India are also expanding participation as production costs and shipping logistics make Southeast Asian manufacturers competitive for regional distribution.

Veterinary pharmaceutical and medical device suppliers represent the second-largest exhibitor category at 40+ vendors. They showcase diagnostic equipment, surgical instruments, prescription diet formulations and pharmaceutical products to clinic chains and individual veterinarians building their product formularies. Live grooming competitions and dog/cat shows drive consumer footfall, positioning grooming and care services as revenue streams for participating veterinary clinics and retail partners.

Industry analysis indicates petfood trade volume across MENA grew 11 percent year-over-year through mid-2026, driven by rising disposable income in Gulf states and expanding pet ownership in urban centres. Export pricing for premium formulations (grain-free, organic-certified) commands 18-22 percent premiums over standard products. The show runs until 14 September.

Market research from the Global Pet Trade Association indicates that MENA petfood imports represent one of the fastest-growing regional markets, with annual import volumes expanding at 8-12 percent annually. The shift toward premium and speciality formulations—including grain-free, organic-certified and breed-specific diets—is driving higher unit pricing and expanding margins for manufacturers and distributors. Regional retailers are increasingly demanding private-label manufacturing partnerships with overseas suppliers, creating contract manufacturing opportunities for established producers.

Logistics and supply chain efficiency remains a critical competitive factor at Pet World Arabia. Manufacturers showcase integrated supply chain solutions combining factory logistics, port handling, customs clearance and inland distribution. Cold chain logistics for wet food products and temperature-sensitive supplements is emerging as a distinct competitive advantage, with dedicated refrigerated container services and specialised warehousing. Participants also discuss sustainability initiatives in packaging reduction, recyclable materials and carbon-neutral shipping options that appeal to environmentally conscious retailers and consumers in Gulf markets.
author: Jakson Gudawela
